topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Pulse and the Wave
lecture_lines: Signals exist in time and frequency domains.
The Fourier Transform decomposes complex signals.
A guitar pluck illustrates this duality perfectly.

sections.title: The Duality Challenge
lecture_lines: Signals narrow in time broaden in frequency.
A brief pulse requires infinite frequencies.
This is the core duality challenge.

sections.title: Mathematical Formulation (The Bound)
lecture_lines: Heisenberg-Gabor sets a fundamental bound.
Uncertainty is not a measurement error.
Wave packets obey this physical law.
Gaussian shapes minimize this uncertainty product.
Squeezing time forces frequency to widen.
animations: Fade in Heisenberg inequality formula (#FFFFFF) centrally.
Highlight spatial variance (#FF3333) with.
Highlight frequency variance (#33FF33) with.
Show product of variances > constant (#FFFF33).
Draw rectangle (#FF5733) showing minimum uncertainty bound.

sections.title: The Optimal Solution: Gabor Atoms
lecture_lines: The Gaussian is the optimal signal.
It acts as a perfect window.
Engineers use it to balance domains.
Detecting short chirps requires this precision.
It provides the ideal processing balance.
animations: Fade in Gaussian function (#FF5733) as envelope.
Animate Gaussian modulating sine carrier (#33FF57).
Scale Gaussian to visualize optimal uncertainty bound.
Overlay "Optimal Gabor Atom" text.
Flash Gabor atom to highlight structural balance.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Modern Communication
lecture_lines: We cannot localize perfectly in both.
Resolution choice depends on specific goals.
Radar systems exemplify this critical trade-off.
Bats use pulses for different tasks.
Choosing resolution governs modern signal processing.
